strings.public.prototype.architecture-atlas.purp: Test one public learning path from registered architecture to a bounded Atlas neighborhood and complete reading leaves.
strings.public.group.architecture.title: How VexLife is structured
strings.public.group.architecture.brief: The stable identities and relationships that keep VexLife understandable as it grows.
strings.public.group.architecture.purpose: Explore the architecture without loading private Home data or requiring an AI model.
strings.public.group.registries.title: Registries
strings.public.group.registries.brief: Stable catalogs that say what exists, who owns it, and how identities relate.
strings.public.group.registries.purpose: See how VexLife prevents features, capabilities, modules, and interface meaning from becoming disconnected copies.
strings.public.group.atlas.title: Atlas
strings.public.group.atlas.brief: A bounded way to traverse registered identities and typed relationships.
strings.public.group.atlas.purpose: Start from one identity, inspect its neighborhood, then follow only relationships that are actually registered.
strings.public.node.blueprint.title: Universal Blueprint
strings.public.node.blueprint.brief: The composed source of stable VexLife product meaning and registered interface relationships.
strings.public.node.registry-compiler.title: Registry Compiler
strings.public.node.registry-compiler.brief: Compiles canonical sources into one stable identity and relationship registry.
strings.public.node.atlas.title: Capability & Tool Atlas
strings.public.node.atlas.brief: Traverses a bounded neighborhood of registered identities without inventing new relationships.
strings.public.node.feature-registry.title: Feature Registry
strings.public.node.feature-registry.brief: Binds each registered feature to its human introduction, state, actions, permissions, modules, tests, platforms, and review lenses.
strings.public.node.capability-registry.title: Capability Registry
strings.public.node.capability-registry.brief: Separates seeing and understanding a capability from permission and execution.
strings.public.leaf.blueprint.what: The Universal Blueprint is the composed definition of VexLife product identity, screens, state domains, actions, Terrain, platforms, components, and registry references.
strings.public.leaf.blueprint.why: It gives browser and native projections one semantic source instead of letting every interface redefine the product.
strings.public.leaf.blueprint.how: Small source-managed fragments are composed into one validated record, then other registries and platform projections consume those stable references.
strings.public.leaf.blueprint.when: Use it when you need to understand the canonical product meaning behind a screen, action, state, or Terrain identity.
strings.public.leaf.blueprint.boundaries: The Blueprint describes canonical meaning. It does not grant runtime authority, private Home access, or public deployment by itself.
strings.public.leaf.blueprint.related: Related architecture includes the Registry Compiler, Feature Registry, Capability Registry, and Atlas.
strings.public.leaf.registry.what: The Registry Compiler turns canonical blueprint, module, process, feature, capability, and other registered sources into stable typed identities.
strings.public.leaf.registry.why: It lets VexLife ask “what is this, who owns it, and what does it connect to?” without relying on file names or duplicated prose.
strings.public.leaf.registry.how: Each source contributes stable refs and typed edges. The compiler validates duplicates and builds a registry that can be queried or projected without changing the underlying owners.
strings.public.leaf.registry.when: Use it when tracing ownership, impact, source, actions, permissions, proof, or neighboring identities.
strings.public.leaf.registry.boundaries: Compiling relationships does not create new product state, authority, or availability. It reflects registered sources.
strings.public.leaf.registry.related: The Atlas traverses the compiled identities; Feature and Capability registries contribute important relationship families.
strings.public.leaf.atlas.what: The Atlas is a bounded traversal over registered identities and typed edges.
strings.public.leaf.atlas.why: It gives a person or Vex a way to learn nearby responsibilities without loading the entire architecture into one view.
strings.public.leaf.atlas.how: A query starts from stable refs or an intent, follows allowed outgoing and reverse edge types, and stops at explicit depth, result, and token budgets.
strings.public.leaf.atlas.when: Use it when you know one concept and want to understand what it relates to, where its proof lives, or which capability or owner is adjacent.
strings.public.leaf.atlas.boundaries: The Atlas does not invent relationships, execute capabilities, or bypass public/private admission. A result is knowledge, not authority.
strings.public.leaf.atlas.related: The Registry Compiler supplies stable relationships; Feature and Capability registries make feature and action boundaries discoverable.
strings.public.leaf.feature.what: The Feature Registry records each product feature once and binds it to the identities needed to explain and prove it.
strings.public.leaf.feature.why: A feature should not become a loose UI card. Registration keeps its human introduction, state, actions, permissions, modules, tests, platforms, and review lenses connected.
strings.public.leaf.feature.how: Feature records reference existing stable owners instead of copying their behavior. Validators reject missing or inconsistent relationships.
strings.public.leaf.feature.when: Use it when asking whether a feature is registered, what introduces it to a person, what proves it, or what remains held.
strings.public.leaf.feature.boundaries: Registered does not mean released, executable, or available on a static public page. Effect authority stays with the referenced owners.
strings.public.leaf.feature.related: Feature records connect naturally to capabilities, modules, states, actions, tests, platforms, and review lenses.
strings.public.leaf.capability.what: The Capability Registry defines what kinds of actions can be discovered, explained, requested, admitted, executed, and completed.
strings.public.leaf.capability.why: It keeps “I can see this exists” separate from “I am allowed and able to execute it.”
strings.public.leaf.capability.how: Each capability carries a stable ref, purpose, default stage, permission, effect class, visible roles, platforms, and resource class.
strings.public.leaf.capability.when: Use it when deciding what Vex or a person can understand now, request later, or execute only inside a qualified local environment.
strings.public.leaf.capability.boundaries: Seeing a capability never grants execution. Static Pages can explain capability truth without becoming an effect surface.
strings.public.leaf.capability.related: Capability state is useful beside Feature registration, Atlas traversal, actions, permissions, roles, and platform qualification.
